problem:
Given the matrix 
$F=[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 12 & 4\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(F).$
worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(F),$ we reduce the matrix $F$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 12 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(V)$ is ${{f}_{1},{f}_{2}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}.
$$
